2. Listen to the conversation

Listen without reading the script the first time. On your second listen, open it if you need a little help.

Show listening script

Police officer: Alright, so one more time, very briefly. What happened? Start with you, Mr. Patel.

Mr. Patel: Sure. I parked my car in the usual spot by the shopping center around noon. It’s a quiet area, and I’ve never had any issues before. When I came back after shopping with my family, the car was gone. The window was broken, and the car was just gone. I thought maybe I’d left it unlocked, but I always lock it. It’s weird. I reported it right away. I’m so surprised to see that someone would even want a rusty old car like mine!

Police officer: OK, Alright, and you, Mr. Reynolds?

Mr. Reynolds: Yeah, it’s a bit of a mess. I parked my wife’s car outside our house around 3 PM. It’s in a safe neighborhood, so I didn’t think anything of it. When she came back home, she asked where her car was. I looked out of the window, and the car just wasn’t there. I didn’t hear the noises or anything. That was one clean job, I gotta admit. But how could two cars be stolen in such different places and then end up together? Such an interesting incident.

Police officer: Thank you both for your statements. If anything else comes to mind, please let us know. Now I need to speak to Ms. Davis.
